comparisons.evidence: The page is warm paper-dominant at all three widths. Navy/black is confined to rules, the selected view and typography rather than becoming a full-page stage.

The Pokémon cover is preserved inside a bounded low-radius rectangular product frame paired with title, environment, author and update metadata. At 1280 the cover and metadata occupy opposite halves of a very wide identity panel; the relationship remains legible but is looser than the source Products grid.
comparisons.advisory: If the experiment advances, cap the identity content width or strengthen the cover/title grouping at desktop without enlarging the card into a hero.

comparisons.evidence: Identity → restrained description → ruled statistics → two-state view switch → collection content → persistent actions is visible and ordered consistently.
Primary panels use approximately 1–4px radii depending on Taro scale, thin 1–2px rules, sparse red/yellow and restrained purple price semantics. No oversized pill language is present.

After mentally masking Pokémon media, names and explicit hues, recognition still comes from paper mass, product-catalog framing, black ruled sections, compact metadata, high-density collection grid and low-radius geometry.

The page translates the source Products system rather than copying its page: bounded product media, editorial labels, ruled metadata and a dense catalog surface are retained while host content and actions remain unchanged.
